subject: DIF Analysis with large MCAR data due to test design

messages.subject: DIF Analysis with large MCAR data due to test design
parts:
Hi

I am trying to run DIF analysis on my test bank containing 93 items that have been administered to over 10k test takers randomly, with each test taker attempting only 7 items. Items are binary, coded as 1 for correct and 0 for incorrect. I need to check for the following
1. What is the reliability of this bank?
2. Are there any DIF items with respect to gender?
Challenge: the data is sparse, so can "mirt" package handle this and compute the required parameters? If yes, then how? Please help. I am really stuck here.

I have run the following commands
#DIF analysis
data<-dummy[,2:95] #questions and gender only
library(difR) #nonIRT method
test1<-difMH(Data= data, group= "Gender", focal.name=1, purify= TRUE, nrIter=25)
plot(test1)
#output not captured

#IRT method of dif analysis

#set the gender variable to categorical
data$Gender<-ifelse(data$Gender==2,"M","F") #converts number to categories, specifying gender==2 suggests that values equal to 2 are male (because we mentioned M first) and after the comma means if its not male, then its female
library(mirt)
test<-multipleGroup(data[,2:94],1,itemtype='2PL',group=data$Gender, SE=TRUE,
                    invariance=c('free_means','free_var'))

I am getting error. Please help me identify the problem in my script.
